review.scope: Source-only review of the draft first-handover system (dispatch_limiter, handover_coordinator, protected_handover broker, protected_writer, handover_runtime, hosted_cycle, operations_report, supplied tests and operator directives). Reviewed for correctness, privacy, authority boundaries, persistent artifacts, fail-closed behavior, identity bindings, recovery semantics, and preservation of scientific approvals. No tests executed; no deployed behavior claimed; supporting modules (job_store, git_publication, public_export, phone_notifications, remote_supervisor, hosted_context) were not supplied and are assumed per their call sites.
findings: BLOCKER handover_runtime.Runtime.model: stage derived from hard-coded ['continuation','review','disposition'][position] while the coordinator dispatches handlers by name and Runtime.recover uses binding['stages'][position]. Coordinator.submit accepts any 1-3 ordered subset of installed handlers, so a legal binding like stages=['review'] executes an Astra continuation stage in place of the Claude review — wrong fixed-role model family — and bookkeeping then crashes on the missing -1.json receipt. Fix: derive stage from binding['stages'][position] and enforce the canonical stage prefix at submit/enqueue.

BLOCKER handover_runtime.Runtime.bookkeeping: no per-task failure isolation and no failure recording. Any COMPLETE task with missing -1/-2 receipts, an exhausted review claim, or a failing Queue.attach raises and aborts bookkeeping for all subsequent tasks on every tick, and the failure path never calls Queue.unavailable (unlike hosted_cycle.run), leaving the review row stuck in REVIEWING. Violates the directive's 'block only the affected task' requirement. Also rescans all COMPLETE tasks with file I/O every tick, unbounded over time.

BLOCKER protected_handover.Broker.stage_status: ignores the <stage>.started.json marker, so a turn folder created but refused before model launch (scan/predecessor/admission/envelope failure after binding.json but before started.json) reports UNCERTAIN_MODEL_RECONCILE_NO_RETRY even though no model provably ran. Combined with the runtime's hard-coded attempt='1' and no supplied operator route to advance attempts, one pre-launch refusal permanently blocks the task. Return a distinct not-started status when started.json is absent, or document the operator reconciliation route.

BLOCKER handover_runtime.Runtime.controls: the outcome receipt is written outside the try/except, so IMMUTABLE_OUTPUT_CONFLICT or OSError on the receipt write aborts all control processing and the whole tick instead of recording a BLOCKED outcome for that single request.

SUGGESTION (acknowledged gap): nightly flow is not executable end-to-end — nothing submits or schedules the enqueue_report binding (no q.submit/q.schedule call, no CLI enqueue operation). Progress doc acknowledges unfinished wiring; must be completed before any activation claim.

SUGGESTION protected_handover.model_stage: max_model_turns budget counts every turn folder ever created, including turns refused before any model call, with no lifecycle or reclamation route; after the cap all turns fail SUPERVISED_MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Intentional supervised bound, but an operator reclamation route should exist before deployment.

SUGGESTION protected_handover.serve: single-threaded request handling stalls status/pause queries behind 240 s model calls; runtime client timeout of 300 s barely covers one stage plus envelope overhead. (Client-timeout-mid-stage recovery itself works correctly: the receipt persists and stage_status retrieves it with zero model calls.)

SUGGESTION minor: dispatch_limiter._admit duplicate path does not persist a first-time policy_sha256 binding; serve's non-activated socket has a brief pre-chmod permission window; a pause applied mid-task takes effect only at the next task's admission gate so up to three 240 s stages continue after pause; controls() silently skips non-64-hex request filenames.

POSITIVE: authority/privacy boundaries hold — CAS ledger validates outgoing bytes pre-write with midnight-latched halt, clock-rollback rejection, and binding-checked duplicate admission; operator reset/initialize unreachable via socket and bound to OS uid; SO_PEERCRED peer check; publication destination/repository pinned constants; writer token scope verified and environment restored before any model spawn; broker errors emit named codes only; completed review survives disposition failure; recovery retrieves hash-verified original receipts with zero model calls.
